title: Odd Even Linked List
prompt:
Given the `head` of a singly linked list, group all nodes at odd positions together followed by all nodes at even positions, and return the resulting list. Positions are 1-indexed (the head is position 1). You must do this in place using the existing nodes, and the relative order inside the odd group and inside the even group must be preserved.

The list is given as an array (e.g. `[1,2,3,4,5]` represents `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> null`). The starter code includes helpers to convert between the array and a linked-list node — build the actual list, rewire it by manipulating `next` pointers, then convert back to an array to return.
constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 10^4]
hints: You want O(1) extra space, so building separate lists and copying values back won't be the ideal approach — think about rewiring pointers directly.
Maintain two separate chains as you walk the list once: one collecting odd-position nodes, one collecting even-position nodes.
After splitting the two chains apart, the odd chain's tail should point to the even chain's head to join them into the final answer.

solution.approach: Maintain two pointers, `odd` and `even`, starting at the first and second nodes respectively, and remember the even chain's head to reattach later. Walk through the list, relinking odd.next to skip to the next odd-position node and even.next to skip to the next even-position node, advancing both pointers each time. Once the traversal reaches the end, the odd chain's tail's next is set to the saved even-chain head, joining the two groups while preserving each group's internal relative order.
